products.name: Ovulation (LH) test strips
products.covers: LH, the hormone that surges before ovulation
products.why: Finds the LH surge that usually comes a day or two before ovulation, to help time sex.
sources: Manders M, et al. Timed intercourse for couples trying to conceive. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2015
MedlinePlus (NIH), Ovulation home test

products.name: Digital Ovulation Test
products.covers: LH, with a digital result
products.why: The same LH check with a digital readout instead of reading lines.
sources: Manders M, et al. Timed intercourse for couples trying to conceive. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2015
MedlinePlus (NIH), Ovulation home test

products.name: Fertility hormone monitor
products.covers: Fertility hormones in urine, read by a small monitor
products.why: Reads hormone levels in urine at home and charts them in an app.
sources: Su HW, et al. Detection of ovulation, a review of currently available methods. Bioengineering & Translational Medicine, 2017

products.name: Fertility monitor
products.covers: Several fertility hormones on one strip
products.why: Reads several fertility hormones from one urine strip with your phone.
sources: Su HW, et al. Detection of ovulation, a review of currently available methods. Bioengineering & Translational Medicine, 2017

products.name: PdG test strips
products.covers: PdG, a progesterone marker in urine
products.why: Checks for a progesterone marker in urine in the days after ovulation.
sources: Su HW, et al. Detection of ovulation, a review of currently available methods. Bioengineering & Translational Medicine, 2017

products.name: Basal body thermometer
products.covers: Basal body temperature, to two decimals
products.why: Reads to two decimals, for charting the small rise that follows ovulation.
sources: Su HW, et al. Detection of ovulation, a review of currently available methods. Bioengineering & Translational Medicine, 2017

products.name: Prenatal multivitamin with folic acid
products.covers: Folic acid and other vitamins for pregnancy
products.why: Folic acid before and in early pregnancy lowers the risk of neural tube defects.
sources: US Preventive Services Task Force, Folic Acid Supplementation to Prevent Neural Tube Defects, 2023
CDC, Folic Acid

products.name: Early Result pregnancy test
products.covers: hCG, the pregnancy hormone
products.why: Home tests detect the pregnancy hormone hCG; a positive is worth confirming with a clinician.
sources: MedlinePlus (NIH), Pregnancy test

products.name: Stelo over-the-counter CGM
products.covers: Glucose, read by a sensor on your arm
products.why: A glucose sensor sold without a prescription in the US, for adults not using insulin.
sources: FDA news release, FDA Clears First Over-the-Counter Continuous Glucose Monitor, March 2024
NIDDK (NIH), Continuous Glucose Monitoring

products.name: Lingo glucose biosensor
products.covers: Glucose, read by a sensor on your arm
products.why: An over-the-counter sensor and app for adults not using insulin.
sources: FDA 510(k) clearance of Abbott's over-the-counter Lingo and Libre Rio systems, June 2024
NIDDK (NIH), Continuous Glucose Monitoring

products.name: CGM, by prescription
products.covers: Glucose, read by a sensor on your arm
products.why: A prescription CGM. Ask your clinician whether it fits you.
sources: NIDDK (NIH), Continuous Glucose Monitoring

products.name: Oura Ring
products.covers: Sleep, heart rate, HRV and temperature
products.why: Reads nightly temperature, heart rate, HRV and sleep; connects to Solia Health.
sources: Maijala A, et al. Nocturnal finger skin temperature in menstrual cycle tracking (Oura ring). BMC Women's Health, 2019

products.name: Apple Watch
products.covers: Heart rate, sleep and wrist temperature on recent models
products.why: Recent models read wrist temperature at night, plus heart rate and sleep, through Apple Health.
sources: MedlinePlus (NIH), Pulse

products.name: Garmin smartwatch
products.covers: Heart rate, HRV and sleep
products.why: Reads heart rate, HRV and sleep; connects through the Fitbit · Garmin · Whoop row.
sources: MedlinePlus (NIH), Pulse

products.name: Fitbit tracker
products.covers: Heart rate and sleep
products.why: Reads heart rate, sleep and, on some models, skin temperature.
sources: MedlinePlus (NIH), Pulse

products.name: Whoop strap
products.covers: Heart rate, HRV, skin temperature and sleep
products.why: A screenless strap that reads heart rate, HRV, skin temperature and sleep.
sources: MedlinePlus (NIH), Pulse

products.name: Menstrual heat wraps
products.covers: Steady heat for period cramps
products.why: Heat on the lower belly eased period cramps in trials.
sources: Jo J, Lee SH. Heat therapy for primary dysmenorrhea: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Scientific Reports, 2018

products.name: Period underwear
products.covers: Absorbs period flow
products.why: Reusable underwear that absorbs flow, for comfort and fewer pads.
sources: No trial evidence; listed as a comfort item

products.name: Menopause-trained clinicians, by video
products.covers: Perimenopause and menopause care by video
products.why: Clinicians who focus on perimenopause and menopause care, including treatment options.
sources: The 2022 Hormone Therapy Position Statement of The North American Menopause Society. Menopause, 2022

products.name: Cooling bedding
products.covers: Bedding that feels cooler
products.why: Bedding made to feel cooler, which some people find helps with night sweats.
sources: No trial evidence; listed as a comfort item

products.name: Digital CBT-I program
products.covers: A self-guided CBT-I course
products.why: Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the first-line treatment for long-term insomnia.
sources: Qaseem A, et al. Management of Chronic Insomnia Disorder in Adults: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians. Annals of Internal Medicine, 2016

products.name: CBT-i Coach app (free)
products.covers: CBT-I tools and a sleep diary
products.why: A free app that guides you through CBT-I steps, best used alongside a clinician.
sources: Qaseem A, et al. Management of Chronic Insomnia Disorder in Adults: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians. Annals of Internal Medicine, 2016

products.name: Thyroid tests you order online
products.covers: Thyroid blood tests, such as TSH
products.why: Thyroid problems can change periods and fertility; a TSH blood test is the usual first check.

evidence.label: Lab test; go over results with a clinician

sources: MedlinePlus (NIH), TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone) Test

products.name: HbA1c blood sugar test you order online
products.covers: HbA1c: your average blood sugar over about three months
products.why: PCOS guidelines advise checking blood sugar from time to time; HbA1c is one common way.

evidence.label: Lab test; go over results with a clinician

sources: Teede HJ, et al. Recommendations from the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome. Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism, 2023
MedlinePlus (NIH), Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) Test

products.name: Women's Fertility Test
products.covers: Reproductive hormones and thyroid (TSH) from a finger-prick sample
products.why: Hormone levels can point to things worth discussing with a clinician, but they can't tell you whether you'll get pregnant.
sources: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine. Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion. Fertility and Sterility, 2020

products.name: Perimenopause Test
products.covers: Hormones such as FSH and estradiol
products.why: Over 45, perimenopause is usually recognised from symptoms; hormone levels swing from day to day, so one test says little.
sources: NICE guideline NG23, Menopause: identification and management (2015, updated 2024)
